text.p: The Globalstar mobile communication system will begin service on January 1, 1999, an official of Alcatel Espace, one of the project's partners and suppliers, said on Wednesday.

Alcatel Espace chairman Jean-Claude Husson also told reporters that financing for the project expected to cost $2.5 billion was nearly all in place. Alcatel Espace is a unit of French electrical engineering group Alcatel Alsthom.

Globalstar will faciliate mobile communication through a system of 48 low-earth-orbiting satellites plus eight back-up satellites. The satellites are to be put into orbit by September 1998, Husson said.
Communications will cost between $1.00 and $1.50, Husson said, adding that the system's break-even point will be at around 2.5 million users.
The Globalstar L.P., based in San Jose, California, was founded by New York high-tech firm Loral Corp and QUALCOMM.

The system is designed to give customers in over 100 countries voice communications as well as data transmission, paging and facsimile services. Customers would use hand-held, vehicle-mounted or fixed site terminals.
